failure_patterns.pattern: strength_mismatch: Selected stronger or broader conclusions based on plausibility rather than establishing every added rate, endpoint, or estimate.

rejected_edits.content: - For a “strongest” or “complete characterization” question, verify each refinement against the exact result: a theorem valid on a stated parameter range does not establish failure outside it, and do not insert a conventional constant that weakens an explicitly normalized bound. Distinguish uniqueness of an object from uniqueness up to isomorphism, scaling, or induced data. When options give different algebraic criteria, check whether they are actually equivalent in the stated class; use small admissible examples to separate them rather than choosing by terminology.
rejected_edits.target: - For an equivalence, check both implications.

rejected_edits.content: - At an infinite endpoint, distinguish the meanings of limsup and liminf: limsup equal to minus infinity means the quantity is eventually below every finite threshold, while liminf equal to minus infinity may only guarantee arbitrarily late subsequential dips. Do not treat these as equivalent unless existence of the full limit is established.
rejected_edits.target: - Preserve the exact form of asymptotic assertions: note cutoffs, the order of iterated limits, and whether the claim uses a limit or limsup. Do not silently replace a truncated approximation with convergence to a full series.
